name: Mounting Plates
function: Structural support for the electronics stack
description: Twin support plates that sandwich the electronics stack, spreading load evenly across the top of the frame and preventing flex under vibration.
howItWorks: Two flat plates sandwich the flight controller and receiver boards between them, spreading clamping force from the deck screws evenly so no single point of the stack flexes under vibration.
learningTip: Look for this pattern in most multirotor frames — a 'sandwich' stack is lighter than a solid enclosure but just as rigid.

name: Plate Fitting Inserts
description: Threaded inserts embedded in the mounting plates, letting the top deck be fastened and removed repeatedly without stripping the frame material.
howItWorks: Metal or reinforced-plastic inserts are set into the plate material so screws can be removed and reinstalled repeatedly without wearing out the threads.
learningTip: Threaded inserts are why you can service a drone dozens of times without the frame loosening up.

name: Top Deck
description: The uppermost plate of the fuselage. The flight controller and GPS module are bolted to its underside, keeping them shielded from the elements.
howItWorks: A rigid plate that caps the electronics stack. The flight controller and GPS module mount to its underside, shielded above by the upper hull.
learningTip: On most builds, this is the first panel a technician removes to access the flight controller.

name: Deck Screws
function: Fastens the top deck to the frame stack
description: Four corner screws that clamp the top deck firmly down onto the frame stack, the first fasteners removed when opening the drone up.
howItWorks: Four corner screws compress the top deck down onto the layers beneath it, distributing clamping force symmetrically.
learningTip: Removing these four screws is usually step one in any teardown.

name: Receiver Mounting Board
function: Isolated mounting shelf for the receiver
description: A small internal shelf that isolates and positions the radio receiver above the main frame, keeping its antenna leads clear of other wiring.
howItWorks: A small internal platform that positions the radio receiver above the main frame, keeping its antenna leads separated from power wiring to reduce interference.
learningTip: Keeping signal wiring away from power wiring is a basic EMI-reduction technique used throughout aviation electronics.

name: Receiver Antenna Port
description: A feed-through connector that routes the receiver's antenna lead outside the fuselage for a clean, unobstructed control-link signal.
howItWorks: Routes the receiver's antenna lead from inside the fuselage to an external position for unobstructed signal reception.
learningTip: Antenna placement matters as much as antenna quality — burying one inside a carbon-fiber shell can block signal entirely.

name: Radio Receiver
description: Picks up control commands transmitted from the pilot's remote and passes them on to the flight controller in real time.
howItWorks: Continuously listens for a radio signal from the transmitter, decodes stick/switch positions, and streams them to the flight controller many times per second.
learningTip: Modern receivers use frequency-hopping to resist interference from other 2.4GHz devices like Wi-Fi.

name: Battery Connector
description: The power port where the battery's discharge lead plugs into the drone, feeding the flight controller and all four motor ESCs.
howItWorks: A high-current connector where the battery's discharge leads plug in, feeding the flight controller and all four motor ESCs from a single point.
learningTip: This connector has to handle the drone's full current draw — it's rated well above normal flight current for safety margin.

name: Flight Battery
description: The removable LiPo pack that supplies flight power. Its placement here, low and central, sets the drone's centre of gravity for stable flight.
howItWorks: A LiPo (lithium-polymer) pack stores the energy for the whole flight. Its physical position is chosen deliberately low and central to set a stable center of gravity.
learningTip: Battery placement affects flight stability as much as motor power does — that's why it always sits near the drone's balance point.

name: Bottom Frame Plate
description: The main lower chassis plate that the arms, landing legs, and body shells all key into — the structural backbone of the airframe.
howItWorks: The lower chassis plate that every other structural part — arms, legs, body shells — keys into. It's the part all flight loads ultimately pass through.
learningTip: If you only reinforce one part of a drone for durability, it's usually this one.

name: Frame Screw Fittings
function: Reinforced anchor points for the frame
description: Reinforced screw bosses moulded into the bottom frame plate, anchoring it securely to the rest of the airframe.
howItWorks: Moulded screw bosses that anchor the bottom frame plate to the rest of the airframe without stress-cracking the surrounding material.
learningTip: Reinforced bosses are why 3D-printed drone frames don't strip their screw holes after a few flights.

name: Mid-Frame Screws
function: Joins upper and lower airframe halves
description: Six screws that fasten the bottom frame to the mid-body assembly, tying the upper and lower halves of the drone together.
howItWorks: Six screws fasten the bottom frame to the mid-body assembly, tying the top and bottom halves of the drone into one rigid unit.
learningTip: Distributing fasteners (six here, not one big screw) spreads mechanical stress and improves crash survivability.

name: Lower Hull
description: The bottom half of the outer shell, enclosing the battery, receiver, and wiring while shielding them from dust and impact.
howItWorks: Encloses the battery, receiver, and internal wiring, shielding them from dust, moisture, and impact from below.
learningTip: Most drone crash damage happens to the lower hull first — it's usually designed to be the most replaceable part.

name: Cooling Vent
description: A louvred opening in the underside of the hull that lets warm air escape from around the motor ESCs and battery bay during flight.
howItWorks: A louvred opening that lets warm air generated by the motor ESCs and battery escape during flight, using natural convection.
learningTip: ESCs and batteries both perform worse when hot — passive venting is a simple, weight-free cooling solution.

name: Upper Hull
description: The top half of the outer shell. Its aerodynamic profile shapes the drone's silhouette and smooths airflow over the fuselage.
howItWorks: Shapes the drone's silhouette and smooths airflow over the fuselage, reducing drag in forward flight.
learningTip: Even small drones benefit from aerodynamic shaping — it directly extends flight time.

name: Gimbal Base
function: Structural anchor for the camera assembly
description: The mount that connects the camera assembly to the underside of the fuselage, providing a stable anchor point for the gimbal handle.
howItWorks: Connects the gimbal/camera handle to the underside of the fuselage, providing a stable, vibration-resistant mounting point.
learningTip: Camera mount rigidity affects video smoothness as much as the gimbal itself does.

name: Gimbal Base Screws
function: Secures the camera base to the hull
description: Four screws securing the gimbal base to the lower hull, keeping the camera assembly rigid relative to the airframe.
howItWorks: Four screws lock the gimbal base rigidly to the lower hull so the camera assembly doesn't shift during flight.
learningTip: Loose camera mounting screws are a common cause of shaky FPV footage.

name: FPV Camera
description: Streams first-person video to the pilot's goggles or monitor, and can record onboard footage during flight.
howItWorks: Streams live video to the pilot's goggles or monitor in real time, and can simultaneously record footage onboard.
learningTip: FPV cameras prioritize low latency over resolution — a delayed video feed is far more disorienting to a pilot than a slightly blurry one.

name: Camera Retaining Screws
function: Locks the camera at a fixed viewing angle
description: Small screws that lock the camera body into its handle bracket at a fixed, vibration-resistant viewing angle.
howItWorks: Small screws clamp the camera body into its handle bracket so the viewing angle stays constant and vibration-resistant during flight.
learningTip: Camera tilt angle is a deliberate pilot choice — more tilt suits high-speed flying, less suits smooth cinematic shots.

name: Landing Legs
description: Four shock-absorbing legs that raise the fuselage off the ground, keeping the spinning propellers clear during takeoff and landing.
howItWorks: Four legs raise the fuselage off the ground, keeping the spinning propellers clear of the surface during takeoff and landing.
learningTip: Landing gear height is a trade-off — taller legs give more prop clearance but raise the center of gravity.

name: Propellers
description: Twin-blade propellers that convert motor torque into thrust. Opposite pairs spin in reverse directions to cancel out rotational torque.
howItWorks: Twin-blade propellers push air downward to generate lift. Opposite pairs spin in reverse directions so their rotational torque cancels out, keeping the drone from spinning uncontrollably.
learningTip: This is the same principle a helicopter's tail rotor solves differently — a multirotor solves it by alternating spin direction instead.

name: Propeller Retention Bolts
description: The central bolts that clamp each propeller firmly onto its motor shaft so it spins true under load.
howItWorks: A central bolt through the propeller hub threads into the motor shaft, clamping the two together so the prop spins true under load.
learningTip: An improperly torqued prop bolt is one of the most common causes of in-flight vibration.

name: Brushless Motors
description: Four independent brushless motors, each driven by its own electronic speed controller, giving the flight controller precise thrust authority on every axis.
howItWorks: Four independent brushless motors, each driven by its own electronic speed controller (ESC), let the flight controller vary thrust on each corner independently — this differential thrust is how the drone steers.
learningTip: A quadcopter has no control surfaces like a plane — literally all steering comes from varying each motor's speed individually.

name: Propeller Lock Nuts
description: Self-locking nuts that keep the propeller retention bolts from working loose under the constant vibration of flight.
howItWorks: Self-locking nuts thread onto the propeller retention bolts, resisting the constant vibration of flight that would otherwise work a plain nut loose.
learningTip: Self-locking (nylon-insert or deformed-thread) nuts are standard anywhere vibration is constant — aircraft, drones, and engines all use them.

name: Propeller Bolt Caps
description: Aerodynamic covers that shield the bolt head from the airstream and smooth airflow over the spinning motor hub.
howItWorks: A shaped cover shields the bolt head from the airstream, smoothing airflow over the spinning motor hub and reducing turbulence.
learningTip: Small aerodynamic details like this add up — hub drag is a real, measurable efficiency loss at speed.

name: Motor Arm Mounts
description: The outer end of each arm, machined to hold a motor perfectly square to its thrust axis for balanced, efficient flight.
howItWorks: The outer end of each arm is machined to hold its motor perfectly square to the intended thrust axis — any misalignment here reduces efficiency and adds vibration.
learningTip: Arm length is a major design lever: longer arms improve stability but increase weight and reduce agility.

name: Arm Mount Screws
function: Secures each motor mount to the frame
description: Four screws per arm — sixteen in total — securing each motor mount firmly to the airframe against constant vibration.
howItWorks: Four screws per arm (sixteen total) clamp each motor mount firmly to the airframe, resisting the constant vibration generated by four spinning motors.
learningTip: Sixteen screws for four motors — that's four fasteners per motor, a deliberate safety margin against any single screw loosening.
